topic: Mastering the Product and Chain Rules in Calculus

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Rates
sections.content: Briefly review the derivative as an instantaneous rate of change. Introduce a visual: a 'Speedometer' showing how the rate of a function changes over time.
sections.example: A cheetah chasing a gazelle: The total distance is a function of the cheetah's speed (f) and the time (g).

sections.title: The Product Rule: Handling Interacting Factors
sections.content: Explain that when two functions multiply, the derivative is not just the product of the derivatives. Use a growing rectangle visualization where both length and width change simultaneously. Formula: (f*g)' = f'g + fg'.
sections.example: A balloon expanding in both width (w) and height (h) simultaneously. Area A = w * h. Change in Area = (Δw)h + w(Δh).

sections.title: The Chain Rule: The 'Nesting' Mechanism
sections.content: Introduce composite functions as 'nested boxes'. Visual: A small gear (inner function) inside a larger gear (outer function). The rate of the whole system is the product of both gears' rates. Formula: f(g(x))' = f'(g(x)) * g'(x).
sections.example: A robotic arm where the movement of the gripper (outer) depends on the rotation of the elbow joint (inner).

sections.title: Integrated Application: Combined Rules
sections.content: Demonstrate a complex function that requires both rules. Provide a step-by-step visual map that breaks down the function into layers and factors.
sections.example: Calculating the velocity of a bio-sensor signal: f(x) = (3x^2) * sin(x^3). We identify the product (first term * second term) and the chain (the sine function's internal power).

sections.title: Conclusion & Mental Check
sections.content: Summarize with a mnemonic: 'Product rule is a dance of pairs; Chain rule is peeling an onion.' Provide a final summary table for quick review.
sections.example: A quick visual animation showing a 'Product Rule Tool' vs. a 'Chain Rule Gear' helping solve a final 10-second challenge problem.
